newsitem.title: USA: Report raps both U.S. and Swiss over Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: Report raps both U.S. and Swiss over Nazi gold.

text.p: A U.S. government study criticized Switzerland on Wednesday for dealing in Nazi gold during World War Two and blamed the Swiss and U.S. governments of the time for their handling of the issue after the war.

The seven-month study also concluded that some of the gold the Nazis took from individual Holocaust victims was melted down and sold to Switzerland along with gold the Nazis looted from occupied governments.
It said that while the Swiss were aware of Nazi gold thefts from other countries, there was no evidence that the Swiss knew they were accepting individual "victim" gold.

"The Swiss were handling vast sums of looted gold" from the Third Reich, said the report, which was compiled by Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat and the State Department's chief historian, William Slaney.

The document criticized the United States for not pushing Switzerland hard enough once the war ended to account for and return the millions of dollars worth of gold it had acquired in financial deals with the Nazis during the war.

But the report said the Swiss were obdurate negotiators, at first denying they had received looted gold, then opposing its return and "using legalistic positions to defend their every interest, regardless of the moral issues also at stake." It

said: "The Swiss contended they had purchased it in good faith, that it was part of war booty obtained in accordance with international legal principles by the Third Reich during its victorious campaigns, and that there was no international legal principle" that would allow the Allies to recover and redistribute it.

"This overall pattern of apparent Swiss bankers' indifference to the needs of the victims of the Holocaust and their heirs persisted until the current international pressure came to bear..." the report said.

Criticizing the weakness of the U.S. efforts at the time, the study said: "There was a demonstrable lack of senior-level support for a tough U.S. negotiating position with the neutrals (neutral countries)," including Switzerland.

Switzerland paid $58.1 million in gold to a commission set up by the Allies after the war. But the report estimated the amount of looted Nazi gold in Swiss hands at the time as between $305 million and $409 million.

Nazi Germany confiscated some $580 million of central bank gold -- around $5.6 billion in today's values -- along with other assets during the war, the report said. It said it was taken from governments and civilians, from Jews and non-Jews murdered in extermination camps, "from whom everything was taken down to the gold fillings of their teeth."

The report said: "Although there is no evidence that Switzerland or other neutral countries knowingly accepted victim gold, the study provides clear evidence ... that at least a small portion of the gold that entered Switzerland and Italy included non-monetary gold from individual civilians in occupied countries and from concentration camp victims or others killed before they even reached the camps."
Some of the gold wound up in the gold pool of the commission set up by the allies after the war to return the looted metal to its rightful owners, the report said.

It said that the remaining amount in the pool today -- about $70 million -- "is small, but if a significant portion of this amount could be given to Holocaust survivors, it would help them live their declining years in dignity."

It said the United States would explore the idea of an international conference on the flow of Nazi assets after the war and said it would be important to have German Reichsbank records available to trace them.
Britain's new Labour government offered on Tuesday to host such a conference, and Switzerland welcomed the idea.

The report also criticized other neutral countries. "It is painfully clear that Argentina, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey and other neutral countries were slow to recognize and acknowledge that this was not just another war. Most never did," it said.
"Whatever their motivation, the fact that they pursued vigorous trade with the Third Reich had the clear effect of supporting and prolonging Nazi Germany's capacity to wage war."
